negative_findings.description: No Diebold Nixdorf case study or success story naming a Hungarian bank was located across the DN case-study hubs and search. Visible European entries were Valiant, FOREX, Sparkasse Hannover, CSOB and similar.
negative_findings.result_summary: DN publishes an extensive named-client library, but no HU client surfaced in this pass. Absence is unconfirmed, not proven — the library is paginated and partly PDF-only.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: DN is a prime ATM/self-service competitor in HU (it maintains a Hungarian legal entity with Budapest and Székesfehérvár sites), so the lack of a public HU reference means its HU install base must be inferred from registry, tender and job-posting signals instead.

negative_findings.description: No Temenos press release or success story naming a Hungarian bank was found, despite targeted queries against the Temenos press and success-story indexes and against named HU candidates (Gránit, MagNet, Erste).
negative_findings.result_summary: Only generic Temenos market/analyst releases surfaced.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: Suggests Temenos may have little or no publicly disclosed Hungarian core-banking footprint; if the Hungarian core-banking layer is served by local/regional players instead, the competitor map for A6 must shift toward local vendors.

negative_findings.description: No Ingenico, Verifone or PAX customer reference, partner page or press release naming a Hungarian bank, acquirer or PSP was found. Results returned only generic terminal-market comparisons and US reseller shops.

negative_findings.why_it_matters: Terminal-supplier mapping in HU cannot rely on vendor case studies and will need acquirer disclosures, certification lists, tender records and MNB/terminal-fleet statistics instead.

negative_findings.description: Hungarian-language queries using esettanulmány / referencia / szállító / rendszerbevezetés / sajtóközlemény returned regulator, banking-association and consultancy content rather than international-vendor case studies. International vendors appear not to publish Hungarian-language customer references at all.

negative_findings.result_summary: Recorded as a high-value lead requiring full-text verification, not as a confirmed HU supplier fact.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: Group-level vendor announcements are routinely over-read as country-level facts; the HU claim must be confirmed against the release text or the local subsidiary before use.

coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Run a dedicated PDF-harvest pass over vendor media directories and text-search the extracted content for Hungary/Hungarian bank names; log gated assets rather than filling forms.

coverage_gaps.description: The strongest confirmed HU vendor evidence clusters in 1997-2020 (Euronet-Budapest Bank, ACI-OTP/Erste/Takarekinfo). Recent 2023-2026 supplier changes — including the MKB/Budapest Bank/Takarék merger into MBH Bank and the reported Brink's acquisition of NCR Atleos — are not yet reflected.
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Re-run vendor newsrooms for 2023-2026 with the post-merger entity names (MBH Bank, Gránit, MagNet, Raiffeisen HU, K&H, UniCredit HU) and track whether legacy Budapest Bank ATM outsourcing carried over to MBH.

coverage_gaps.description: Snowballing surfaced non-listed vendors relevant to HU (valantic at Erste Bank Hungary; Capsys and T-Systems Magyarország as ACI delivery partners), showing the eleven-vendor cell definition understates the actual HU supplier landscape.
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Expand the cell's actor map with local and mid-tier vendors and treat each newly named supplier as a new pointer node to crawl.

brief: For Hungary, international vendor customer-reference material is highly uneven: payments software and ATM outsourcing vendors publish rich named-client evidence, while hardware terminal and security vendors publish essentially none. The two anchor sources are ACI Worldwide's IR newsroom (OTP Bank Group, Erste Bank Hungary, Takarekinfo, plus the ACI/Capsys/T-Systems claim of ~75% of HU real-time payments) and Euronet's IR archive (Budapest Bank ATM outsourcing since 1997, ABN AMRO Hungary, Bank Austria Creditanstalt); Finastra (Raiffeisen core retail) and NCR Atleos (Budapest ATM manufacturing plant) are secondary anchors, while Diebold Nixdorf, Temenos, Ingenico, Verifone, PAX, INETCO and Thales yielded no HU-named public reference in this pass. Hungarian-language search did not produce vendor case studies at all — its value was in surfacing the local delivery layer (Capsys, T-Systems Magyarország), HU legal entities of the vendors, and local trade press that names implementation suppliers. Collection should therefore centre on scheduled crawls of vendor IR/newsroom indexes plus newswire and trade-press mirrors, with local-language integrator and registry sources used to corroborate and to snowball beyond the original vendor list.
